polities.name: Ava Kingdom
polities.note: Upper Burma; Prome vassal until 1482, Toungoo vassal until 1510. Ruled by Mohnyin-led Shan confederation 1527-1555; fell to Toungoo 1555.

polities.name: Hanthawaddy Kingdom
polities.note: Mon kingdom of Lower Burma; fell to Toungoo 1538-1539.

polities.name: Restored Hanthawaddy Kingdom
polities.note: Mon revolt against Toungoo; sacked Ava 1752; destroyed by Alaungpaya 1757.

polities.name: Launggyet Dynasty
polities.note: Arakanese kingdom before Mrauk U; overrun by Ava 1406, Arakan contested Ava/Pegu 1406-1429.

polities.name: Mrauk U Kingdom
polities.note: Restored with Bengal Sultanate help 1429 (Bengal tributary to c. 1531). Held Chittagong c. 1459-1666 (lost to Mughals). Conquered by Konbaung 1785.

polities.name: Prome Kingdom
polities.note: Broke from Ava 1482; conquered by Toungoo 1542.

polities.name: Toungoo Empire
polities.note: Toungoo was a vassal of Ava until 1510. Expansion: Pegu 1539, Ava 1555, Shan states 1557, Lan Na 1558, Ayutthaya 1564/1569, Lan Xang 1565-74. Collapsed 1599.

polities.name: Restored Toungoo Kingdom
polities.note: Re-unified Burma incl. Shan states; Lan Na vassal 1614-1727. Lower Burma lost to Mon revolt 1740; Ava fell 1752.

polities.name: Konbaung Dynasty
polities.note: Arakan annexed 1785; Manipur/Assam 1814-1826. Lost Arakan & Tenasserim 1826, Lower Burma 1852; annexed by Britain 1885.

polities.name: British Burma
polities.note: Colonial. 1826-1852 Arakan (separately, from Akyab) and Tenasserim; 1852 Lower Burma; 1886 all Burma; Shan states as protectorates.

polities.name: Mong Kawng
polities.note: Northernmost Shan state (Kachin hills/upper Irrawaddy). Burmese occupation 1477, 1651-1742, 1771-1775; annexed 1796. Ming pacification office nominally.

polities.name: Mohnyin
polities.note: Shan state; its sawbwa Sawlon and son Thohanbwa led the Shan confederation that took Ava 1527. Vassal of Toungoo from 1557; absorbed into Burma early 17th c.

polities.name: Hsenwi
polities.note: Largest northern Shan state; Burmese vassal from 1557 with lapses; split into North and South Hsenwi under British 1888.

polities.name: Hsipaw
polities.note: Northern Shan state; earlier origins legendary. Burmese vassal from 1557; British protectorate 1887.

polities.name: Kengtung
polities.note: Tai Khun state east of the Salween; Lan Na sphere until 1558, then mostly Burmese vassal; British 1890.

polities.name: Mong Nai
polities.note: Leading southern Shan state; Burmese vassal from 1557; Burmese viceroy seat at Mong Nai in Konbaung era.

polities.name: Yawnghwe
polities.note: Southern Shan state around Inle Lake; Burmese vassal from 1557.

polities.name: Mong Mit
polities.note: Northern Shan state; Burmese vassal from 1557.

polities.name: Lawksawk
polities.note: Western Shan state; Burmese vassal.

polities.name: Karenni States
polities.note: Independent in the 18th c.; split into five principalities (Kantarawaddy largest) in 19th c.; independence recognised by Britain and Burma 1875; British tributary 1892.

polities.name: Sipsongpanna
polities.note: Tai Lue kingdom; dual tributary to China (Ming/Qing) and Burma from the 1560s.

polities.name: Kale
polities.note: Shan state in the Kabaw/Myittha valley, contested with Manipur and Ava; absorbed by Burma (dates uncertain).

polities.name: Lan Na
polities.note: Northern Tai kingdom; Burmese vassal 1558-1775 (de facto independent 1727-1763; Chiang Mai under Burmese governors after 1578).

polities.name: Kingdom of Chiang Mai (Rattanatingsa)
polities.note: Siamese vassal under the Chet Ton (Kawila) dynasty; Chiang Mai depopulated 1776-1797 (court at Lampang/Pa Sang); absorbed into Monthon Phayap 1899.

polities.name: Lampang
polities.note: Principality of the Thipchang/Chet Ton line; Burmese then (from 1775) Siamese vassal.

polities.name: Nan
polities.note: Annexed to Lan Na 1449; Burmese vassal 1558-1788; Siamese vassal 1788-1931.

polities.name: Phrae
polities.note: Lan Na/Burmese then Siamese vassal; princely rule ended after the 1902 Shan rebellion.

polities.name: Sukhothai Kingdom
polities.note: Ayutthaya vassal from 1378; seat at Phitsanulok in the last decades; absorbed 1438.

polities.name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
polities.note: Burmese vassal 1564/1569-1584; destroyed by Konbaung 1767. Malay tributaries (Patani, Kedah, Kelantan, Terengganu) and Cambodia intermittently.

polities.name: Thonburi Kingdom
polities.note: Taksin's reunification of Siam; Lan Na, Vientiane, Luang Prabang, Champasak and Cambodia brought under suzerainty 1774-1779.

polities.name: Rattanakosin Kingdom
polities.note: Direct core plus Khorat plateau (Isan, annexed after 1828). Vassals listed separately: Lan Na principalities, Luang Prabang, Vientiane (to 1828), Champasak, Cambodia, northern Malay sultanates. Lost left-bank Laos 1893, western Cambodia 1907, Kedah/Kelantan/Terengganu/Perlis 1909.

polities.name: Nakhon Si Thammarat
polities.note: Southern Thai mueang ruled by hereditary governor-kings; independent 1767-1769 under Chao Nakhon; supervised Siam's Malay tributaries; absorbed into monthon system 1896.

polities.name: Lan Xang
polities.note: Capital moved to Vientiane 1560; Burmese suzerainty c. 1574-1597; split into Luang Prabang and Vientiane 1707 (Champasak 1713).

polities.name: Kingdom of Luang Prabang
polities.note: Siamese vassal 1779-1893; French protectorate 1893-1947 (became Kingdom of Laos).

polities.name: Kingdom of Vientiane
polities.note: Siamese vassal from 1779; destroyed after Anouvong's revolt 1827-1828 and annexed by Siam.

polities.name: Kingdom of Champasak
polities.note: Siamese vassal from 1778; left bank to France 1893, remainder 1904; royal line continued as governors.

polities.name: Muang Phuan
polities.note: Tai Phuan principality on the Plain of Jars; tributary to Lan Xang, then by turns Vientiane, Luang Prabang, Siam and Vietnam (annexed by Vietnam as Tran Ninh 1832, restored later); French 1893/1899.

polities.name: Sipsong Chau Tai
polities.note: Federation of Black/White Tai muang in NW Vietnam under the Deo family at Lai Chau; tributary to Dai Viet and Luang Prabang; French 1888.

polities.name: Khmer Empire
polities.note: Extent shown for c. 1400 (much reduced); Angkor abandoned after Ayutthaya's 1431 sack.

polities.name: Kingdom of Cambodia (post-Angkor)
polities.note: Mekong delta lost to Vietnamese settlement 1623-1780s; Battambang/Siem Reap to Siam 1795; Vietnamese occupation 1835-1840 (Tay Thanh); French protectorate 1863.

polities.name: Champa (Vijaya)
polities.note: Cham kingdom centred on Vijaya; lost Quang Nam to the Ho 1402-1403 (retaken 1407); Vijaya conquered by Le Thanh Tong 1471.

polities.name: Panduranga
polities.note: Rump Champa after 1471; Nguyen vassal from 1697 as Thuan Thanh tran; annexed by Minh Mang 1832.

polities.name: Jarai Kings of Fire and Water
polities.note: Ritual Jarai chieftaincies of the Central Highlands exchanging gifts with Cambodia and the Nguyen; little territorial control (see gaps for highlands).

polities.name: Ho Dynasty
polities.note: Usurped Tran 1400; took Champa's Quang Nam 1402-1403; destroyed by Ming invasion 1407.

polities.name: Ming Jiaozhi
polities.note: Province of Ming China; Le Loi's Lam Son uprising controlled much of the south from 1418-1426.

polities.name: Later Le Dynasty (Early Le)
polities.note: Expanded to Vijaya 1471. Le emperors restored nominally 1533-1789 under the Trinh (see Trinh lords).

polities.name: Mac Dynasty
polities.note: Held Tonkin north of Thanh Hoa against the restored Le/Trinh (Southern Court) 1533-1592; Ming tributary; remnant in Cao Bang 1592-1677.

polities.name: Trinh Lords (Restored Le, Dang Ngoai)
polities.note: Le emperors restored 1533 in Thanh Hoa, with the Trinh as hereditary regents from 1545; retook Thang Long 1592; border with Nguyen at the Gianh river from 1627; ended by Tay Son 1786 (Le emperor to 1789).

polities.name: Nguyen Lords (Dang Trong)
polities.note: Southern realm nominally under Le; independent de facto from 1600/1627. Took Kauthara 1653, Panduranga suzerainty 1697, Gia Dinh (Saigon) 1698, Ha Tien vassal 1708, Mekong delta by 1757. Destroyed by Tay Son 1777.

polities.name: Tay Son Dynasty
polities.note: Brothers Nhac (Quy Nhon), Hue (Phu Xuan) and Lu (Gia Dinh); took Tonkin 1786-1788; Gia Dinh lost to Nguyen Anh 1788; destroyed 1802.

polities.name: Ha Tien
polities.note: Chinese-led port polity founded by Mac Cuu; Cambodian then (from 1708) Nguyen vassal; sacked by Siam 1771; absorbed into Vietnam after 1809.

polities.name: Nguyen Dynasty
polities.note: Unified Vietnam; Cambodian protectorate 1811-1847 (annexed 1835-1840). Lost Cochinchina 1862-1867; French protectorate (Annam, Tonkin) 1883-1945.

polities.name: French Cochinchina
polities.note: French colony: three eastern provinces 1862, all six 1867.

polities.name: Malacca Sultanate
polities.note: Ming tributary 1405-1435; hegemon of the peninsula (Pahang, Kedah, Terengganu, Johor/Riau) and Sumatran coast (Kampar, Indragiri, Siak, Rokan) by 1470s. Taken by Portugal 1511.

polities.name: Portuguese Malacca
polities.note: Fortified colonial city with small hinterland.

polities.name: Dutch Malacca
polities.note: VOC/Dutch possession (British occupation 1795-1818); ceded to Britain 1824/1825.

polities.name: Straits Settlements
polities.note: British: Penang 1786, Province Wellesley 1800, Singapore 1819, Malacca 1824, Dindings 1874; combined 1826, crown colony 1867. Discontinuous: use 25-40 km around each.

polities.name: Johor Sultanate
polities.note: Successor of Malacca; Pahang held as appanage 1623-1853 (listed separately). Bendahara dynasty from 1699; Bugis Yang Dipertuan Muda dominant 1722-1784; split by the 1824 Anglo-Dutch treaty.

polities.name: Johor (Temenggong Sultanate)
polities.note: Temenggong Daeng Ibrahim given mainland Johor 1855; Abu Bakar Maharaja 1868, Sultan 1885; British adviser 1914.

polities.name: Riau-Lingga Sultanate
polities.note: Island rump of Johor under Dutch protection; Bugis viceroys at Penyengat; abolished by the Dutch 1911.

polities.name: Pahang Sultanate
polities.note: Old sultanate 1470-1623 (Malacca then Johor sphere; Ayutthaya claims); appanage of the Johor Bendahara 1623-1853; independent under Bendahara Ali 1853, sultanate 1882; British protectorate 1888.

polities.name: Kedah Sultanate
polities.note: Old Malay sultanate; Siamese tributary (bunga mas) for long periods; Penang ceded 1786; Siamese occupation 1821-1842; Perlis detached 1843; to British 1909.

polities.name: Perlis
polities.note: Detached from Kedah by Siam 1843; Siamese tributary to 1909, then British.

polities.name: Perak Sultanate
polities.note: Founded by a Malacca prince; Acehnese domination 1575-1640s; Dutch tin monopoly posts 17th-18th c.; Siamese pressure 1818-1826; British Resident 1874 (Pangkor).

polities.name: Selangor Sultanate
polities.note: Bugis-founded sultanate; British Resident 1874. Royal seats Kuala Selangor, later Klang/Jugra.

polities.name: Negeri Sembilan
aliases: Rembau, Sungai Ujong, Johol, Jelebu, Sri Menanti
polities.note: Minangkabau-derived confederation of luak (Sungai Ujong, Jelebu, Johol, Rembau, etc.) under a Yang di-Pertuan Besar from 1773 (Raja Melewar); British protection 1874-1895.

polities.name: Patani Kingdom
polities.note: Malay sultanate; queens' era 1584-1688 was its commercial peak. Ayutthaya tributary intermittently; conquered by Siam 1786 and split 1808 into seven mueang.

polities.name: Seven Malay Provinces of Patani
aliases: Pattani, Nongchik, Yaring, Yala, Raman (Reman), Ra-ngae (Legeh), Saiburi (Teluban)
polities.note: Seven Malay-ruled mueang under Songkhla supervision; Reman and Legeh held inland/southern parts. Raja rule abolished 1902.

polities.name: Kelantan Sultanate
polities.note: Malacca vassal (1460s-1511), later in Patani's orbit; modern Long Yunus dynasty from 1760/1764; Siamese tributary to 1909, then British. Seat Kota Bharu from 1844 (earlier Kota Kubang Labu nearby).

polities.name: Terengganu Sultanate
polities.note: Founded by a Johor prince (Sultan Zainal Abidin I); Siamese tributary (bunga mas) c. 1782-1909, then British.

polities.name: Samudera Pasai Sultanate
polities.note: Early Muslim port-state of north Sumatra; Majapahit raids 1350s; Portuguese fort 1521; absorbed by Aceh 1524.

polities.name: Pedir
polities.note: Pepper port-kingdom between Aceh and Pasai, briefly dominant c. 1500; absorbed by Aceh 1521-1524.

polities.name: Aceh Sultanate
polities.note: Absorbed Lamuri, Pedir, Pasai by 1524; peak under Iskandar Muda 1607-1636 held both Sumatran coasts to Padang and Deli/Aru plus peninsula vassals (Pahang, Kedah, Perak, Johor briefly). Aceh War from 1873; Dutch conquest substantially complete 1903.

polities.name: Aru Kingdom
polities.note: Karo/Malay-ruled east-coast kingdom; contested by Aceh and Johor in the 16th c.; finally subdued by Aceh 1613; succeeded by Deli.

polities.name: Deli Sultanate
polities.note: Founded by an Acehnese commander; independent of Aceh 1669; under Siak influence c. 1770-1858; Dutch 1862; capital moved to Medan 1891.

polities.name: Langkat Sultanate
polities.note: Malay principality of NE Sumatra; Aceh then Siak spheres; Dutch contract 1869.

polities.name: Serdang Sultanate
polities.note: Split from Deli 1723; Dutch 1865.

polities.name: Asahan Sultanate
polities.note: Founded by an Acehnese prince; Siak influence late 18th c.; Dutch 1865.

polities.name: Siak Sri Indrapura
polities.note: Founded by Raja Kecil (claimant to Johor); at its 1780s-1810s height dominated the east Sumatran coast from Tamiang to Indragiri; Dutch 1858.

polities.name: Indragiri Sultanate
polities.note: Malay river kingdom; Malacca then Johor tributary; Dutch contract 1838.

polities.name: Jambi Sultanate
polities.note: Pepper sultanate on the Batang Hari; VOC post 1615; wars with Johor 1660s-1680s; Dutch protectorate 1833/1858; resistance under Sultan Taha to 1904.

polities.name: Palembang Sultanate
polities.note: Javanese-descended rulers from c. 1527 (Demak/Mataram tributary); sultanate proclaimed 1659/1675; controlled Bangka tin; abolished by the Dutch 1823 after 1819-1821 wars.

polities.name: Pagaruyung Kingdom
polities.note: Minangkabau royal seat (Yang Dipertuan); real power in autonomous nagari; the 'rantau' coast held by Aceh 1600s and the VOC from 1663. Royal family killed by the Padri 1815; Dutch annexation 1833.

polities.name: Padri State
polities.note: Reformist Islamic movement controlling much of the Minangkabau highlands; Bonjol fell to the Dutch 1837.

polities.name: Inderapura Sultanate
polities.note: Pepper sultanate on the SW Sumatran coast; Aceh then VOC influence; absorbed by Dutch 1792.

polities.name: Barus
polities.note: Camphor port with two rival royal houses (Hulu and Hilir); Aceh then VOC suzerainty; Dutch 1840.

polities.name: Toba Batak (Sisingamangaraja)
polities.note: Toba Batak priest-kings of Bakkara with ritual authority over autonomous marga villages (huta/bius); resistance to Dutch 1878-1907. Karo, Pakpak, Simalungun and Angkola-Mandailing Batak listed in gaps/Simalungun.

polities.name: Simalungun kingdoms
polities.note: Several small Simalungun Batak rajadoms (seven by the 19th c.); Dutch control 1907.

polities.name: Bencoolen
polities.note: English East India Company pepper settlement; ceded to the Netherlands 1824.

polities.name: Lampung marga chiefdoms
polities.note: Pepper-producing clan (marga/buay) federations under Banten suzerainty from the 1530s; Dutch from 1808, resistance (Raden Intan) to 1856.

polities.name: Majapahit
polities.note: Direct rule over East and Central Java (and Madura, Bali); nominal claims across the archipelago (Nagarakretagama). Paregreg civil war 1404-1406; north-coast ports broke away to Demak in the late 15th c.; court at Daha (Kediri) under Girindrawardhana from c. 1478; ended c. 1527.

polities.name: Sunda Kingdom
polities.note: Hindu kingdom of West Java; lost Cirebon (1480s), Banten and Sunda Kelapa (1527) to Muslim states; Pakuan destroyed by Banten 1579.

polities.name: Cirebon Sultanate
polities.note: Founded by Sunan Gunung Jati; Mataram vassal from c. 1619; split 1677 into Kasepuhan, Kanoman (and later Kacirebonan) under VOC protection from 1681.

polities.name: Demak Sultanate
polities.note: First Muslim power of Java; took over Majapahit's heartland c. 1527; Trenggana's death 1546 led to fragmentation; succeeded by Pajang.

polities.name: Pajang Sultanate
polities.note: Interior successor of Demak under Jaka Tingkir (Hadiwijaya); supplanted by Mataram.

polities.name: Mataram Sultanate
polities.note: Conquered Surabaya 1625 and Madura 1624; peak under Sultan Agung (to 1645). Trunajaya revolt 1674-1680 made it dependent on the VOC; ceded north coast 1743/1746; partitioned at Giyanti 1755.

polities.name: Surakarta Sunanate

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Half of Mataram after Giyanti 1755 (lands interlaced with Yogyakarta); outer provinces (mancanegara) annexed after the Java War 1830.

polities.name: Yogyakarta Sultanate

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Other half of Mataram (Hamengkubuwana); British sack 1812; Java War 1825-1830 (Diponegoro).

polities.name: Mangkunegaran

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Junior principality carved from Surakarta lands by the Treaty of Salatiga 1757 (Wonogiri, Karanganyar).

polities.name: Banten Sultanate
polities.note: Pepper sultanate of West Java with Lampung as dependency; destroyed Pajajaran 1579; VOC protectorate after 1682-1684; abolished by Raffles 1813.

polities.name: Dutch Java (VOC and Dutch East Indies)
polities.note: Directly ruled territory on Java only (outer-island posts and protectorates are noted under each polity): Batavia and Ommelanden 1619; Priangan 1677-1705; north coast 1743-1746; East Java/Blambangan 1768-1772; nearly all Java except the Vorstenlanden after 1830. British interregnum 1811-1816.

polities.name: Blambangan
polities.note: Last Hindu kingdom of Java's eastern salient; often under Balinese (Gelgel, Buleleng, Mengwi) suzerainty; Mataram attacks 1639; conquered by the VOC 1767-1772.

polities.name: Surabaya
polities.note: Leading East Javan port-state after Majapahit, heading a coalition of coastal states (also claiming Sukadana in Borneo); conquered by Mataram 1625.

polities.name: Tuban
polities.note: Majapahit-era port that became an independent Muslim principality; taken by Mataram 1619.

polities.name: Giri Kedaton
polities.note: Theocratic principality of the Sunan Giri line at Gresik with wide religious influence (Maluku, Lombok); destroyed by Mataram/VOC 1680.

polities.name: Madura (West) / Bangkalan

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: West Madura principality (Arosbaya/Sampang, later Bangkalan) under the Cakraningrat dynasty from 1624; Mataram vassal, then VOC (from 1705/1743); abolished 1885.

polities.name: Sumenep

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: East Madura principality; Mataram vassal 1624-1705, then VOC/Dutch; abolished 1883.

polities.name: Gelgel (Bali)
polities.note: Javanese-descended kingdom ruling all Bali; at its 16th-c. peak (Dalem Baturenggong) also Blambangan, Lombok and west Sumbawa. Weakened from 1651 (Gusti Agung Maruti); court moved to Klungkung 1686.

polities.name: Klungkung
polities.note: Seat of the Dewa Agung, nominal paramount of Bali; holds Nusa Penida; puputan and Dutch conquest 1908.

polities.name: Buleleng
polities.note: North Bali kingdom of Panji Sakti; held Blambangan c. 1697-1730; under Karangasem early 19th c.; Dutch expeditions 1846-1849; direct Dutch rule 1882.

polities.name: Karangasem
polities.note: East Bali kingdom; conquered west Lombok in the 1670s-1740s (see Mataram Lombok); Dutch protectorate after 1894.

polities.name: Mengwi
polities.note: Powerful 18th-c. west-central Bali kingdom (held Blambangan c. 1730-1767); destroyed and partitioned by Badung, Tabanan and Gianyar 1891.

polities.name: Badung
polities.note: South Bali kingdom; Dutch conquest and puputan 1906.

polities.name: Tabanan
polities.note: West-central Bali kingdom; Dutch conquest 1906.

polities.name: Gianyar
polities.note: Founded c. 1771; accepted Dutch protection 1900 (continued as self-governing regency).

polities.name: Bangli
polities.note: Interior Bali kingdom (Batur highlands); Dutch protectorate 1908.

polities.name: Jembrana
polities.note: Thinly peopled west Bali kingdom, often dependent on Buleleng/Mengwi; Dutch rule from 1849/1882.

polities.name: Selaparang
polities.note: Main Sasak Muslim kingdom of Lombok (others: Pejanggik, Langko); Gowa/Makassar influence 17th c.; conquered by Balinese Karangasem c. 1740.

polities.name: Mataram (Lombok)
polities.note: Balinese dynasty from Karangasem ruling Lombok (and, after 1849, Karangasem itself); Dutch conquest 1894.

polities.name: Bima Sultanate

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: East Sumbawa sultanate also claiming Manggarai (W Flores) and parts of Sumba; Gowa vassal until 1669; VOC treaty 1669.

polities.name: Sumbawa Sultanate

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: West Sumbawa sultanate (Dewa Dalam Bawa dynasty), Gowa-linked; VOC treaty 1674.

polities.name: Dompu

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Small central Sumbawa sultanate; Gowa then VOC overlordship.

polities.name: Tambora and Pekat
polities.note: Small kingdoms on the Sanggar peninsula wiped out by the 1815 Tambora eruption (Sanggar survived, later merged with Bima).

polities.name: Larantuka (Topass domain)
polities.note: Portuguese-Catholic rajadom of East Flores/Solor and base of the mestizo Topasses (Larantuqueiros), who dominated Timor's sandalwood trade (Lifau HQ) in the 17th-18th c.; sold to the Dutch 1859.

polities.name: Manggarai
polities.note: West Flores; contested by Bima and Gowa (17th-18th c.), Todo-Pongkor lineage paramount by the 19th c.; Dutch 1907.

polities.name: Sikka
polities.note: Catholic rajadom of central-east Flores linked to Portuguese/Larantuka; Dutch from 1859.

polities.name: Ende
polities.note: Muslim coastal rajadom (Bima/Gowa ties) with Lio hinterland chiefdoms; Dutch 1907-1910.

polities.name: Wehali
polities.note: Ritual centre of the Tetun/Belu realms of central Timor; its maromak oan held nominal paramountcy over eastern Timor liurai; Portuguese/Dutch contest, Dutch 1906.

polities.name: Sonbai

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Paramount Atoni kingdom of west Timor; split 1658 into Greater Sonbai (inland, under Topass/Portuguese influence) and Little Sonbai (near Kupang, VOC ally).

polities.name: Amarasi

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: SW Timor kingdom, Portuguese/Topass ally until 1749, then VOC.

polities.name: Dutch Kupang
polities.note: VOC fort and Timorese allies' land (Helong, Little Sonbai, Rote/Sabu islanders); direct control mostly limited to the Kupang bay area until 1900s.

polities.name: Portuguese Timor
polities.note: Governor at Lifau (Oecusse) 1702-1769, then Dili; effective control limited to coastal forts and allied liurai until the 1890s-1912 campaigns. Border with Dutch Timor fixed 1859/1914.

polities.name: Bruneian Sultanate
polities.note: North Borneo thalassocracy; 16th-c. peak claimed the whole NW-N coast (Sarawak to Sabah), parts of Sulu and Manila (to 1571). Lost NE Borneo to Sulu 1704, Sarawak to Brooke 1841-1890, Labuan 1846, Sabah to North Borneo Co 1877-1881; British protectorate 1888, Resident 1906.

polities.name: Raj of Sarawak
polities.note: Brooke dynasty; grew from the Sarawak river (1841) by Brunei cessions: Batang Lupar/Saribas 1853, Rajang-Mukah-Bintulu 1861, Baram 1882, Limbang 1890, Lawas 1905. British protectorate 1888.

polities.name: Sambas Sultanate
polities.note: Malay sultanate (Brunei-descended line) of NW Borneo; Chinese mining kongsi in its hinterland; Dutch contract 1818.

polities.name: Tanjungpura / Matan / Sukadana

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies (Banten claim ceded)

polities.note: Old SW Borneo kingdom (Majapahit tributary); Sukadana a diamond port subdued by Mataram 1622; capital shifted among Sukadana, Matan and Tanjungpura; split into Matan, Simpang and Sukadana (Niew Brussel 1828).

polities.name: Landak

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Diamond-rich upriver kingdom of West Borneo; under Banten-claimed suzerainty, then Dutch (1778/1818).

polities.name: Mempawah

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Bugis-led panembahan (Opu Daeng Menambun) on the coast north of Pontianak.

polities.name: Sanggau
polities.note: Malay-Dayak kingdom on the middle Kapuas; other Kapuas states (Sekadau, Sintang, Selimbau) further upriver.

polities.name: Sintang
polities.note: Upper-middle Kapuas Malay kingdom with Dayak tributaries; Dutch contract 1822.

polities.name: Pontianak Sultanate

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Founded by Syarif Abdurrahman Alkadrie at the Kapuas-Landak confluence; VOC ally from 1779.

polities.name: Lanfang Republic
polities.note: Hakka gold-mining kongsi federation at Mandor; nominal tributary of Pontianak; dissolved by the Dutch 1884.

polities.name: Heshun Kongsi
polities.note: Federation of Chinese mining kongsi (Thaikong dominant) in Sambas' hinterland; defeated in the Kongsi Wars 1850-1854.

polities.name: Kotawaringin Sultanate
polities.note: Founded by a Banjar prince; Banjar dependency, then Dutch (1826).

polities.name: Negara Daha
polities.note: Hindu-Javanese kingdom of the Banjar region, Majapahit tributary; superseded by the Banjar Sultanate 1526.

polities.name: Banjar Sultanate

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Pepper sultanate of SE Borneo; claimed suzerainty over the south and east coast (Kotawaringin, Paser, Kutai, Berau) in the 17th c.; Dutch protectorate 1787; abolished 1860 (Banjarmasin War to 1905).

polities.name: Kutai Martadipura
polities.note: Successor of the ancient Kutai kingdom on the middle Mahakam; conquered by Kutai Kartanegara c. 1635.

polities.name: Kutai Kartanegara Sultanate
polities.note: Lower Mahakam kingdom, Islamised c. 1575; absorbed Martadipura c. 1635 (upper Mahakam Dayak areas only loosely held); capital Kutai Lama, then Pemarangan 1732, Tenggarong 1782; Dutch 1844/1863.

polities.name: Paser Sultanate
polities.note: SE Borneo sultanate with Bugis settler influence; Banjar suzerainty claims; Dutch 1844/1906.

polities.name: Berau
polities.note: NE Borneo kingdom split c. 1810 into Gunung Tabur and Sambaliung (both at Tanjung Redeb); Sulu influence 18th-19th c.; Dutch 1834/1844.

polities.name: Bulungan Sultanate
polities.note: Kayan-descended sultanate of NE Borneo dominating Tidung chiefdoms (Tarakan, Sesayap); Berau then Sulu sphere; Dutch 1850.

polities.name: British North Borneo
polities.note: Chartered company state on lands leased from Brunei and Sulu (1877-1878); British protectorate 1888. Before 1881 see Brunei and Sulu.

polities.name: Iban (Sea Dayak)
polities.note: Acephalous longhouse society; migrated from the Kapuas into the Batang Lupar/Saribas/Skrang basins (16th-17th c.) and expanded into the Rajang in the 18th-19th c.; brought under Brooke rule 1840s-1900s.

polities.name: Kenyah-Kayan
polities.note: Stratified chiefdoms (paramount aristocrats) of the Apo Kayan plateau and the upper Kayan, Mahakam, Baram and Rajang rivers.

polities.name: Ngaju Dayak
polities.note: River-basin peoples of the Kahayan, Kapuas and Katingan in central Borneo; Banjar trade dependence; Tumbang Anoi peace 1894 under Dutch auspices.

polities.name: Gowa Sultanate

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Twin kingdom with Tallo; Islam 1605; by 1640s hegemon of South Sulawesi with overseas dependencies (Bima, Sumbawa, Buton, Selayar, east Borneo coast). Defeated by the VOC and Bone (Bongaya 1667, Somba Opu 1669); VOC vassal after.

polities.name: Bone Sultanate

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies (ally, later suzerain)

polities.note: Leading Bugis kingdom; conquered by Gowa 1611/1643; under Arung Palakka (1672-1696) VOC-backed hegemon of South Sulawesi; Dutch wars 1824-1825, 1859-1860; conquered 1905.

polities.name: Wajo
polities.note: Bugis elective monarchy (Arung Matoa) with strong trading diaspora; Gowa ally until 1670 (Tosora sacked by Bone/VOC); under Bone 1670-1737; La Maddukelleng's revival 1737.

polities.name: Luwu
polities.note: Oldest Bugis kingdom (iron trade, Gulf of Bone); seat at Malangke until c. 1620, then Palopo; dominated by Bone after 1500s; Dutch 1905.

polities.name: Soppeng
polities.note: Bugis kingdom, member of the Tellumpocco alliance with Bone and Wajo (1582).

polities.name: Ajatappareng
polities.note: Confederation of five Bugis kingdoms around Lake Sidenreng and the Parepare coast; Gowa sphere in the 17th c.

polities.name: Mandar confederation

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Seven estuary kingdoms (Pitu Baqbana Binanga) led by Balanipa, allied with seven upland states (Pitu Ulunna Salu).

polities.name: Buton Sultanate

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies (ally/suzerain)

polities.note: Island kingdom (sultanate from 1541) between Gowa and Ternate; VOC ally from 1613; held Muna and parts of SE Sulawesi intermittently.

polities.name: Muna
polities.note: Island kingdom contested by Buton, Ternate and Gowa.

polities.name: Konawe
polities.note: Tolaki kingdom of SE Sulawesi (Mekongga at Kolaka is its western sister); Buton/Bone influence.

polities.name: Gorontalo

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Union of five kingdoms led by Gorontalo and Limboto; Ternate suzerainty in the 16th-17th c.; VOC from 1677; direct Dutch rule 1889.

polities.name: Bolaang Mongondow

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: North Sulawesi kingdom; Spanish/Ternate contacts, VOC treaty 1694; capital moved to Kotamobagu 1901.

polities.name: Minahasa

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies (ally)

polities.note: Confederation of walak chiefdoms; alliance with the VOC (Manado fort) 1679 against Bolaang Mongondow; closely administered by the Dutch from the 1820s-1880s.

polities.name: Banggai
polities.note: Island-and-coast kingdom of east Sulawesi; Ternate vassal; Dutch 1907.

polities.name: Sangihe kingdoms

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Small island kingdoms between Sulawesi and Mindanao; Siau was Catholic and Spanish-allied until the VOC took it 1677; others Ternate tributaries.

polities.name: Ternate Sultanate

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Clove sultanate; core = Ternate, Moti, north and west Halmahera, Makian; at its 1570s-1600s peak (Babullah) claimed 72 islands incl. Hoamoal/Ambon, Buru, Sula, Banggai, Gorontalo and Manado coasts. Spanish held the fort 1606-1663; VOC vassal from 1683.

polities.name: Tidore Sultanate

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Rival of Ternate; held south and east Halmahera (Weda, Maba, Patani) and claimed Raja Ampat and the Papuan coast (tribute/hongi raids). Spanish ally 1606-1663; VOC vassal from 1667; Prince Nuku's revolt 1780-1805.

polities.name: Bacan Sultanate

overlord.name: Dutch East India Company / Dutch East Indies

polities.note: Smallest of the four Moluccan sultanates (Bacan islands, Obi); Ternate and VOC influence.

polities.name: Jailolo Sultanate
polities.note: West Halmahera sultanate, conquered by Ternate and the Portuguese 1551; revived briefly under Tidore patronage c. 1797-1832.

polities.name: Banda (orang kaya confederation)
polities.note: Nutmeg islands governed by councils of orang kaya (Lonthor and Neira leagues) with no single king; conquered and depopulated by the VOC 1621.

polities.name: Hitu
polities.note: Muslim confederation of the north Ambon (Hitu) peninsula under four perdana and a Kapitan Hitu; Ternate ally; subdued by the VOC in the Hitu War 1643-1646.

polities.name: Dutch Amboina
polities.note: Portuguese fort 1576-1605, then VOC seat of the Moluccas (Ambon, Lease islands, west Seram after 1656 Hoamoal war).

polities.name: Sulu Sultanate
polities.note: Sulu archipelago, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi, south Palawan; NE Borneo ceded by Brunei 1704 (leased to the North Borneo Co 1878). Spanish protectorate 1851/1878; US 1899; sovereignty ended 1915.

polities.name: Maguindanao Sultanate
polities.note: Pulangi delta sultanate; peak under Kudarat (1619-1671) holding SW Mindanao coasts from Zamboanga to Davao gulf; later eclipsed by upriver Buayan; Spanish control of Cotabato 1861; US 1905.

polities.name: Buayan Sultanate
polities.note: Upriver rival of Maguindanao on the Rio Grande de Mindanao; strongest under Datu Uto (1860s-1890s); US conquest 1905.

polities.name: Lanao sultanates
polities.note: Confederation of Maranao sultanates around Lake Lanao in four pangampong (Unayan, Masiu, Bayabao, Baloi); resisted Spain and the US.

polities.name: Kingdom of Maynila
polities.note: Muslim polity at the Pasig mouth linked to Brunei (Rajah Sulayman); taken by Legazpi 1571.

polities.name: Tondo
polities.note: Lakan-ruled polity north of the Pasig with Bulacan/Pampanga ties; under Spain from 1571; Tondo Conspiracy 1587-1588.

polities.name: Rajahnate of Cebu
polities.note: Port polity of Rajah Humabon (Magellan 1521) and Tupas; submitted to Legazpi 1565.

polities.name: Butuan
polities.note: Early trading polity of NE Mindanao (Agusan); declined by the 16th c.

polities.name: Caboloan (Pangasinan)
polities.note: Pre-Hispanic Pangasinan polity on the Agno; subdued by Spain c. 1571-1580.

polities.name: Spanish Philippines
polities.note: Effective rule over lowland Luzon and the Visayas and north Mindanao coasts; Cordillera, Mindanao Muslim lands and much of Palawan/Mindoro interior outside control until the 19th c. (Zamboanga fort 1635/1718; Jolo 1876; Cotabato 1861). British occupation of Manila 1762-1764.

polities.name: First Philippine Republic
polities.note: Revolutionary state controlling most of lowland Luzon and the Visayas outside Manila 1898-1899; defeated in the Philippine-American War (Aguinaldo captured 1901).

polities.name: Raja Ampat kingdoms
polities.note: Four petty rajadoms (Waigeo, Salawati, Misool/Lilinta, Waigama) owing tribute to Tidore; Dutch suzerainty via Tidore.

polities.name: Onin petty kingdoms (Fakfak)
polities.note: Small Muslim rajadoms of the Onin/Bomberai peninsula trading slaves and massoi with Seram and Tidore; Dutch post at Fakfak 1898.

polities.name: Kaimana (Sran/Namatota)
polities.note: Rajadoms of the Kowiai coast linked to Seram traders and Tidore; Dutch Fort Du Bus nearby 1828-1836.

polities.name: Dutch New Guinea (posts)
polities.note: Claim west of 141E (1828, via Tidore); Fort Du Bus 1828-1836; administrative posts at Manokwari and Fakfak only from 1898, Merauke 1902. Effective control coastal.

polities.name: British New Guinea
polities.note: Protectorate 1884, colony 1888, Australian Territory of Papua 1906; effective control coastal.

polities.name: German New Guinea (Kaiser-Wilhelmsland)
polities.note: Mainland NE New Guinea (Bismarck Archipelago not included here); company rule 1885-1899; effective control coastal.

polities.name: Palu valley kingdoms
polities.note: Kaili rajadoms of the Palu valley (Sigi, Palu, Banawa, Tawaeli, Dolo); Bugis/Ternate influence; Dutch contracts late 19th c.

gaps.area: Chin Hills and Naga Hills (Burma-India borderlands)
gaps.note: Autonomous Chin chiefdoms (Falam, Haka, Tashon, Sizang) and Naga village polities; no state. British conquest 1889-1890.

gaps.area: Kachin Hills beyond Mogaung, and the Wa/Lahu hills east of the Salween
gaps.note: Jinghpaw duwa chieftaincies (gumsa/gumlao) and Wa village states; nominally inside Ming/Qing and Burmese spheres. Can be filled with Mong Kawng / Hsenwi / Kengtung or left as tribal land.
Bahnar, Sedang, Jarai, Rhade, Mnong, Katu and other highland peoples outside state control (Jarai ritual kings listed). Short-lived 'Kingdom of Sedang' 1888-1890 (adventurer Mayrena).

gaps.area: Cardamom and Dangrek ranges; Khorat plateau north-east interior before 1700
gaps.note: Thinly populated forest; nominally Cambodian/Lan Xang. Pear and Kuy forest peoples.

gaps.area: Malay Peninsula interior (Titiwangsa range, Taman Negara)
gaps.note: Orang Asli (Semang, Senoi, Jakun) rainforest; nominally inside Perak, Pahang, Kelantan, Terengganu.

gaps.area: Sumatra highlands and islands: Gayo/Alas, Karo, Pakpak, Mandailing-Angkola Batak, Kerinci, Rejang-Lebong, Pasemah; Nias, Mentawai, Enggano
gaps.note: Village federations and adat polities (Karo urung, Kerinci depati, Pasemah sumbai) without single rulers; Gayo/Alas nominally Acehnese; Nias and Mentawai stateless. Dutch conquest mostly 1840s-1910.

Deep rainforest: Kadazan-Dusun and Murut (Sabah), Bidayuh (Sarawak), Punan/Penan nomads, Ot Danum, Maanyan; Iban, Kenyah-Kayan and Ngaju listed as tribal nations. Coastal sultanates' authority stopped near the river mouths.

gaps.area: Central Sulawesi and Toraja highlands; Tolitoli/Buol
gaps.note: Sa'dan Toraja, Pamona (Poso), Mori and Bada highlanders with no overarching state (tongkonan/village federations); Buol and Tolitoli small coastal rajadoms.

gaps.area: Lesser Sundas minor islands: Sumba, Solor-Alor-Lembata, Rote, Sabu, Wetar, Tanimbar
gaps.note: Sumba: many small rival chiefdoms (Kodi, Lamboya, Mangili etc.); Solor/Adonara Watan Lema (coastal) vs Paji (inland) leagues; Rote's nusak (18-19 domains) under VOC Kupang; Sabu domains; Alor and Wetar stateless.

gaps.area: Maluku periphery: Seram interior, Buru, Kei, Aru, Halmahera interior
gaps.note: Alune/Wemale/Nuaulu (Seram), Buru clans, Kei ratschap federations (Ur Siw / Lor Lim), Aru villages; nominally under Ternate/Tidore or VOC Ambon/Banda.

gaps.area: Philippines interior: Cordillera Central, Sierra Madre, Mindoro, Palawan, Negros/Panay interior, central and eastern Mindanao
gaps.note: Igorot (Ifugao, Bontoc, Kalinga, Ibaloi), Agta, Mangyan, Palaw'an and Lumad (Manobo, Bukidnon, Bagobo, T'boli, Mandaya) peoples outside Spanish and Moro control until the late 19th c.

gaps.area: New Guinea interior and most of the coast
gaps.note: Stateless societies throughout (highlands, Sepik, Asmat, Marind-anim, Trans-Fly). Only the Raja Ampat/Onin/Kowiai rajadoms (Tidore network) and 1884+ colonial coastal posts are polities. Biak/Numfor raiding networks owed loose tribute to Tidore.
